source_text: Per legem bonam et per mandatum sanctum pravorum animi ferocierant; quoniam sine voluntate propria nulla eruditio poterat inspirare virtutem
pass_a_gloss: Through law bonam and through commandment holy pravorum animi ferocierant; quoniam without by-will own no learning poterat inspirare virtue.

lemmas.lexica: LS lex; Blaise lex Dei / sacred Law
LS voluntas=will, wish; Blaise moral will

pass_b_english: The apostle emphasizes the power of habit.
Through the good law and the holy commandment, the minds of the wicked had become more savage, because no instruction could instill virtue without their own willing participation.

The law is holy, and the commandment holy and just and good. Has what is good, then, become death for me? Certainly not! But sin, so that it might appear as sin, worked death in me through what is good, so that sin might become sinful beyond measure through the commandment. (Romans 7:12–13)

choices.why: Julian's definition of sin is an act of will. Keep 'will' rather than later 'free will' system language unless liberum arbitrium is present.
Julian means Scripture's legal/authoritative witness, especially the divine Law as teacher of justice.
rejected: natural law (unless the sentence is philosophical)

choices.why: Image of God in the soul; keep soul not 'mind' or 'life-force'.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.
